_comment: Аргументы workflow docs/workflows/implement_review_fix.js, которыми выполнялся этап 1 ТЗ v2 (задачи 1.1-1.3). {repo} и {scratch} подставляет сам скрипт из args.repo и args.scratch.

tasks.spec:
TASK 1.1 (class A): diagnostics script for an existing run, computed from saved scores without training.
BRANCH_NAME = wf/s1-diagnostics

Deliverables:
(1) New module src/stad/diagnostics.py — pure, unit-testable functions (no CLI, no printing).
(2) New thin CLI scripts/diagnose_run.py (same sys.path pattern as scripts/run_benchmark.py) that calls a single entry point stad.diagnostics.run_diagnostics(...).
(3) New tests tests/test_diagnostics.py on synthetic data (make_synthetic_corridor), fast (< ~60 s total).

Context you must use (do not reimplement): stad.eventlog.event_table (per-event credit table, already committed: credit.mean() == cell padf), stad.metrics (evaluation_view, make_calibration, threshold_from_calibration, threshold_at_alarm_rate, confirm_alarms, contiguous_segments, eval_segments, full_report, padf), stad.metrics.stats.paired_bootstrap_test, stad.report.compare_to_reference, stad.runner.run_config, stad.baselines.controls.RandomScorer, stad.experiment.ExperimentConfig/build_datasets, stad.registry.get_grid/REFERENCE.

CLI: python scripts/diagnose_run.py --config configs/ft_aed_cv.yaml --run-dir reports/ft_aed_cv --out <dir> [--random-seeds 200] [--n-boot 10000] [--oracle-rates 0.25 1.0] [--recompute-nontrainable] [--tz-reference] [--datasets fold0 fold1 ...]
--run-dir defaults to cfg.out_dir. Required inputs in run-dir: runs.csv. Optional: manifest.json, events.csv, scores/<config>__<dataset>__seed<k>.npy and ...__calib.npy (names exactly as stad.runner saves them).
Outputs in --out: DIAGNOSTICS.md plus CSVs (alarm_units.csv per cell, alarm_units_summary.csv per config, random_null.csv, random_band.csv, model_free.csv, seed_variance.csv, pairwise.csv, reproduction.csv, oracle_rates.csv). Recomputed score arrays (if any) go to <out>/scores_recomputed/ as .npy (these are gitignored).

IMPORTANT REALITY: in this container the pilot runs reports/ft_aed_cv and reports/ft_aed_cv_both have runs.csv/curves.csv/manifest.json but NO scores/ (binaries were not committed). The FT-AED data IS available at {repo}/data/ft-aed (configs resolve "root: data/ft-aed" relative to the current working directory). So the script must degrade gracefully: compute everything that needs only data + runs.csv, optionally recompute scores of NON-trainable cells (--recompute-nontrainable: configs whose registry Config is not trainable, or has randomize_only=True, i.e. ctrl_random, base_*, ctrl_untrained) via stad.runner.run_config with checkpoint_dir=None and device cpu, and clearly list in DIAGNOSTICS.md which cells/sections lack scores and must be re-run on a machine that has scores/ (the user's machine). Recomputed cells must be checked against runs.csv: write reproduction.csv with padf_runs, padf_recomputed, threshold_runs, threshold_recomputed, abs diffs; flag mismatches. Note in the report: ctrl_untrained recomputation is NOT expected to be bit-identical, because in the original runner the untrained weights were initialised before set_seed (init depends on global RNG order of the original run).

What to compute (TZ section 1 items 2-5 must be reproducible from these):
A. Alarm units (TZ 1.3). Definitions: after evaluation_view (node reduction), a cell is a confirmed false alarm if confirm_alarms(s > thr, persistence, segments) & (y == 0) — exactly the numerator of metrics.alarms_per_hour; an "alarm window" is a window with any such cell; an EPISODE is the start of a contiguous run of alarm windows within one segment (contiguous_segments / eval_segments), i.e. alarm[t] and not (alarm[t-1] and same segment). No merge-gap here (that is class-B task 2.1, not yours). Per cell with scores: threshold recalibrated from calib scores exactly like the runner (make_calibration + threshold_from_calibration with the run's alarm_budget_per_hour, persistence, node_reduce) and compared with runs.csv threshold; on test: alarm cells/h (must equal runs.csv alarms_per_hour), alarm windows/h, episodes/h, test hours; on the calibration sample: hours, number of alarm windows and episodes at that threshold (what the threshold actually rests on). Summary per config: mean/min/max of windows/h and episodes/h, nominal budget.
B. Random null and band (TZ 1.2). For each fold, seeds 0..N-1 (N >= 200 by default) of RandomScorer exactly as the grid uses it (RandomScorer(seed).score / .score_calib) -> full_report -> padf, event_recall, alarms_per_hour, plus episodes/h. Seeds 0..k-1 must reproduce runs.csv ctrl_random rows exactly (report the check). Band: expected padf = mean over folds x seeds; Monte Carlo (fixed seed, >= 20000 reps) of the run mean when each fold contributes n_seeds_run independent draws (n_seeds_run = number of seeds in runs.csv) -> 2.5/97.5% quantiles; ALSO the variant with 1 draw per fold (a deterministic config like base_pca has only one independent value per fold: its 5 seeds are identical) -> quantiles; also per-block quantiles. Classify each config mean padf from runs.csv against both band variants (below / inside / above). Known values on the crash pilot (computed by the orchestrator): expected 0.10416; 5-draws-per-fold MC band about [0.057, 0.162]; 1-draw-per-fold about [0.011, 0.239]. The TZ states [0.040, 0.186] — the report must show both variants and say that the TZ interval lies between them (definition not stated in TZ), so classification of configs near the boundary (PCA 0.163, flow 0.167) depends on the band definition.
C. Oracle equal-real-rate diagnostic (TZ 1.3, last dash): threshold_at_alarm_rate on the TEST normals (ORACLE, diagnostic only) at each --oracle-rates value, for each random seed (summarise mean padf) and for every cell with scores; label every such column/section ORACLE and state it is never used for ranking. TZ says random at 1.0/h gives padf 0.355.
D. Model-free scores (TZ 1.4): per window, mean over nodes of standardized occupancy at the LAST time step of the window ("occ_mean"), and minus mean over nodes of standardized speed at the last step ("neg_speed_mean"); feature indices from data.feature_names ("occupancy", "speed"); broadcast to [n, N] so evaluation_view max-reduction returns the same value; test from X_test and calibration from X_calib (same protocol as models). full_report -> average_precision, roc_auc_reference_only, padf, alarms_per_hour (+ episodes/h). Compare with runs.csv means of average_precision and roc_auc_reference_only for every config. TZ numbers: occupancy AP 0.351 ROC 0.702; reference 0.363/0.707; PCA 0.377/0.710; untrained 0.360/0.688.
E. Seed pseudo-replication (TZ 1.5): from runs.csv, per config the within-fold SD of padf across seeds (max over folds) and number of distinct values per fold; flag configs with zero within-fold variance (TZ: base_pca, base_snd, base_california, ctrl_untrained).
F. Paired comparisons vs reference (stad.registry.REFERENCE) side by side, for every config: (i) block bootstrap over dataset x seed blocks from runs.csv (reuse stad.report.compare_to_reference); (ii) fold-level paired bootstrap with seeds averaged within fold (paired_bootstrap_test on 4 values); (iii) cluster bootstrap by EVENT: per (config, dataset, event_id) mean credit over seeds (credits from events.csv if present in run-dir, else computed from scores via stad.eventlog.event_table with the recalibrated threshold), difference to the reference per event, resampling events with replacement STRATIFIED by fold (each fold keeps its event count), statistic = mean difference over all events; 95% CI, two-sided p = min(1, 2*min(P(b<=0), P(b>=0))), half-width. Report the minimal detectable effect = half-width of the event-level CI. Configs without credits are skipped and listed. TZ numbers: block CI for base_iforest vs reference [+0.073, +0.200]; event-cluster CI [+0.024, +0.257]; event-level half-widths 0.10-0.15 for all pairs.
G. DIAGNOSTICS.md (Russian, same style as RESULTS.md / SENSITIVITY.md; use a small markdown table helper like stad.sensitivity._md, do not depend on tabulate): header (run dir, run commit from manifest, config, number of cells with saved scores / recomputed / missing), one section per item A-F, a reproduction section, and "Чего не хватает" listing missing cells and which numbers are therefore absent, with the exact command to re-run on a machine with scores/. With --tz-reference add a reconciliation table "ТЗ v2 §1 -> пересчёт" listing each TZ number above (store them in a module-level constant dict with a comment that these are the reference values from docs/TZ_PROTOCOL_V2.md section 1 for the crash pilot), the recomputed value, abs diff, and status: "совпадает до 3-го знака" / "расходится" / "нет score". Do not write any conclusions about architectures; this is protocol diagnostics.

Tests (tests/test_diagnostics.py), at minimum: 10 consecutive alarm windows = 1 episode; two runs separated by a non-alarm window = 2 episodes; a run crossing a segment boundary = 2 episodes; confirmed windows inside events (y==1) are not counted; alarm cells/h equals metrics.alarms_per_hour on the same inputs; random null seeds 0..1 reproduce run_config of a random baseline exactly; cluster bootstrap: identical credits -> diff 0 and CI [0,0], constant +0.1 shift -> diff 0.1 inside CI, stratification preserves per-fold event counts; model-free scores shape/broadcast and a clear error without an occupancy feature; one end-to-end test: tiny run_grid on synthetic into tmp_path (ctrl_random + a cheap baseline + the reference config cand_gcngru_recon with epochs=1 and a small param budget, 2 seeds) then run_diagnostics on it with a small number of random seeds and n_boot -> DIAGNOSTICS.md and the CSVs exist and alarm cells/h match runs.csv. Use a synthetic ExperimentConfig object (no YAML file needed) — design run_diagnostics to accept an ExperimentConfig plus already-built datasets so tests do not need files.

Finally, sanity-run the CLI on the real crash pilot WITHOUT touching reports/: from cwd {repo} run python <your-worktree>/scripts/diagnose_run.py --config configs/ft_aed_cv.yaml --run-dir reports/ft_aed_cv --out {scratch}/diag_check_s1 --random-seeds 200 --recompute-nontrainable --tz-reference  (it may take ~10-20 min on CPU; if too slow, first try --datasets fold0). Report the key numbers you got (random expected padf and both bands, model-free AP/ROC, zero-variance configs, reproduction diffs, iforest block CI) in your summary.

TASK 1.2 (class A): the runner saves a per-event table.
BRANCH_NAME = wf/s1-events

The runner must write reports/<run>/events.csv with columns exactly, in this order: config, dataset, seed, event_id, t_report, detected, delay_min, credit — one row per test event per successful cell (config x dataset x seed), for freshly computed AND resumed cells.

Use the already-committed helper stad.eventlog.event_table(scores, data, threshold, *, half_life_min, persistence, node_reduce) (read src/stad/eventlog.py and tests/test_eventlog.py). The threshold must be the calibrated one already in the cell row (row["threshold"]); do not recalibrate and never use test labels. Do NOT change the return signatures of run_config or resume_cell (other code and tests unpack 5-tuples): compute the table in run_grid right after a cell succeeds (both branches have the test scores at hand: resume_cell returns them as the 3rd element). A failed cell produces no rows. Write events.csv next to runs.csv (utf-8, index=False) even when save_scores is False; include the DataFrame in the returned dict under key "events". Undetected events: delay_min empty/NaN, credit 0.
Update the runner module docstring (list of artifacts) and the artifacts list in README.md (around the lines listing runs.csv / curves.csv / scores/) to mention events.csv and what it is for (event-level statistics, TZ v2 tasks 1.2/2.4). Do not touch docs/PROTOCOL.md.
Do not touch report.py, checkpoints, train.py, or resume timing (another agent changes resume_cell timing and test_resume.py in parallel — avoid editing resume_cell and tests/test_resume.py to prevent merge conflicts; edit only run_grid and the docstring in runner.py).

Tests in a NEW file tests/test_events_csv.py (synthetic make_synthetic_corridor, small): run_grid with a random baseline, an snd baseline and one tiny trainable config (gcn_gru + recon, epochs=1, small param budget), seeds (0, 1), into tmp_path. Assert: events.csv exists with exactly the column order above; for every cell, sum(credit) / number of events == padf in runs.csv for that cell (abs 1e-12) — this is the acceptance test from the TZ; row count per cell == n_events; detected count == n_detected; then rerun with resume=True (trainable cell restored) and assert events.csv is identical (pd.testing.assert_frame_equal after sorting). Also assert the returned dict has "events".

TASK 1.3 (class A): blocking of conclusions in stad.report.decide and write_results_md, plus timing of resumed cells, plus a script that rebuilds a report from an existing run directory (needed for the stage-1 exit: rebuilding the pilot reports).
BRANCH_NAME = wf/s1-report

Background: in both pilot runs R0 failed, yet sections 3-5 of RESULTS.md printed R1-R7 conclusions ("главный результат", "главный аргумент"). DECISION_RULES.md requires: R0 blocks everything; R1 blocks R2-R7; R3 needs the extended grid. Look at reports/ft_aed_cv/RESULTS.md and reports/ft_aed_cv_both/RESULTS.md to see the problem.

Implement in src/stad/report.py (this file is NOT gated):
(1) decide(runs, *, metric="padf", reference=REFERENCE, checks=None): if checks is None, compute them with validate_protocol(runs, prevalence=mean of runs["prevalence"] if present, else NaN) so the gate cannot be forgotten. If any critical check failed: keep every rule entry's "finding" (numbers are fine) but replace every "action" with exactly "не оценивается: R0 провален", add "status": "blocked_r0", and prepend an entry for R0 listing the failed checks with an action that only says conclusions are not drawn until the protocol is fixed (no chapter actions). The existing power pseudo-rule entry also gets the blocked action in that case.
(2) If R0 passed: R1 computed and "отрыв НЕ значим" -> R1 keeps its own action (that is the rule's outcome), and R2-R7 keep findings but action becomes "заблокировано R1: ..." (short reason: depth does not pay off, choosing between deep architectures is not the subject — DECISION_RULES priority 2), "status": "blocked_r1". If R1 cannot be evaluated in this run (no base_pca or no reference) -> R2-R7 likewise blocked with reason "R1 в этом прогоне не оценён". Every entry gets a "status" key ("ok" when not blocked).
(3) R3 only on a full encoder x head cross: add a helper (e.g. full_cross(runs)) that takes rows with encoder and head not null and group != "control" (so ctrl_untrained is excluded), and accepts it only if every (encoder level, head level) pair is present; if not, try the subset of configs whose names are in stad.registry.EXTENDED; if neither is a full cross -> R3 entry with a finding stating how many of E x H pairs are present and action "не оценивается: требует сетки extended", status "needs_extended". When a full cross exists, compute eta^2 on that subset only. Leave axis_importance (used by figure 04) unchanged, but in RESULTS.md section 4 add a note when the grid is not a full cross: the eta^2 table is descriptive and R3 is not evaluated.
(4) validate_protocol: the "Случайный score: padf у пола" detail text must use the run's actual budget (runs["alarm_budget_per_hour"]; if several values list them; add an optional keyword parameter alarm_budget_per_hour that overrides). Do not change any check threshold or criticality.
(5) write_results_md: pass the checks to decide; when R0 failed, section 3 keeps the numeric columns (diff, CI, p) but the verdict column shows "не оценивается (R0)"; section 5 shows the blocked entries (status visible). Add an optional parameter (e.g. source_note: str | None) that replaces the first "Сгенерировано автоматически ..." sentence for rebuilt reports.
(6) Timing of resumed cells. In stad/runner.py: run_config saves "train_seconds" and "inference_ms_per_window" into the checkpoint "extra" dict; resume_cell restores them from describe(ckpt) when present, else NaN; add a runtime column "timing_source" with values "measured" (run_config, both trainable and baseline branches), "checkpoint" (restored), "missing" (old checkpoint without timing). Edit only run_config and resume_cell in runner.py (another agent edits run_grid in parallel). In report.rank_table add n_timed = count of non-NaN inference_ms_per_window per config; in the RESULTS.md table print the ms/window value with a trailing "*" when n_timed < n_runs (and "—" when 0), with a footnote under the table: "* — среднее по k из n клеток: остальные возобновлены (--resume) без замера времени" (state k and n per config or generically). This must also work for OLD runs.csv files that lack timing_source (the pilots). Update tests/test_resume.py: the assertion that train_seconds is NaN after resume becomes "train_seconds restored equals the first run's value and timing_source == 'checkpoint'"; add a test where the checkpoint extra lacks the timing keys (strip them with torch.load/torch.save of the checkpoint file) -> NaN and "missing".
(7) New script scripts/rebuild_report.py: --run-dir <dir with runs.csv, curves.csv, manifest.json, experiment_config.json> --out <dir> [--metric padf]. Rebuild RESULTS.md with the CURRENT report code from the saved tables (no training, no data, no scores needed), with source_note "Пересобрано из <run-dir> (прогон коммита <sha from manifest>) кодом коммита <current short sha>; числа не пересчитывались, изменены только блокировки выводов (ТЗ v2, задача 1.3)". Regenerate the figures/tables that need only runs.csv and curves.csv (fig01, fig02, fig04, fig05, fig06, fig07, fig09) into <out>/figures and <out>/tables: refactor stad.experiment.make_figures minimally so that datasets=None (or missing scores) skips fig03 (PR curves) and fig08 (event trace) instead of failing; build the ExperimentConfig from <run-dir>/experiment_config.json with out_dir overridden. Do NOT run it on reports/ (the orchestrator will run it after merging); test it on a synthetic run in tmp_path.

Tests in a NEW file tests/test_report_blocks.py (build fake runs DataFrames like _fake_runs in tests/test_protocol.py, and remember the power check "Мощность: критическая разница меньше размаха рангов" is critical): (a) R0 failed (ctrl_random padf above most configs) -> every non-R0 entry from decide has action "не оценивается: R0 провален"; write_results_md output section 5 contains no chapter actions (assert that no "**Что делать.**" line other than the blocked/STOP ones exists, and that strings like "ГЛАВН" and "глав" do not appear in section 5) and section 3 verdicts are "не оценивается (R0)"; (b) R0 passes but reference vs base_pca not significant -> R1 action is the negative-result action, R2-R7 actions start with "заблокировано R1"; (c) R0 and R1 pass on a core-like (non-crossed) grid -> R3 is "требует сетки extended"; with a full cross added (fake ext_* rows) R3 is computed; (d) padf-floor detail mentions the run's budget 0.25 and not "1 тревога/ч"; (e) rank_table/markdown timing star with NaN timings; (f) rebuild_report on a tiny synthetic run directory (create it with stad.runner.run_grid in tmp_path, epochs=1) produces RESULTS.md with the source note.
Make sure existing tests (tests/test_protocol.py etc.) stay green.
